text.p: Finnish beverages maker Oy Hartwall Ab said on Thursday its profitability would continue to develop positively.
"We estimate that the profitability of the Hartwall group will continue its present positive trend," Hartwall said in a statement with its 1996 results.
Hartwall's 1996 profit after financial items rose to 207.5 million markka from 45.7 million the previous year.
Hartwall said soft drinks and mineral water sales would continue to grow in Finland.
Per capita consumption of beer in Finland has risen, but the sales trend is the reverse "owing to Finland's excessively high beer tax," Hartwall said.
"We expect measures by the authorities to lower the beer tax in the very near future...," it said.
The company's five-year agreement on the manufacture, distribution, sales and marketing of Coca Cola products in Finland would continue up to March 15, it said.
"Negotiations on continuing the co-operation are still in progress," Hartwall said.
It said the group's overseas growth prospects were promising as there are over 200 million consumers in the market where its Baltic Beverages Holding Ab joint-venture operates.
Sales by BBH -- owned by Hartwall and Swedish-Norwegian Pripps Ringnes -- are expected to approach 500 million litres this year, Hartwall said.
"The capital spending on plant and equipment to increase the capacity of the new breweries will not be seen in sales volumes to the full extent until 1998," it said.
